balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet: investment assets, liabilities, equity
balanceSheet.content:
An insurer's balance sheet is dominated by the investment portfolio funding policyholder liabilities (insurance contract liabilities, the bulk of total liabilities here), with total equity (incl. NCI) the residual capital buffer.

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: total assets were RMB702.8bn at H1 FY2026 against equity of only RMB61.9bn (~8.8% of assets) -- ordinary leverage ratios built for operating companies understate the gearing an insurer carries by design; the regulator's solvency ratios (comprehensive 196%, core 136% at FY2025, both down from 227%/158%) are the leverage metric that matters, not a debt/equity ratio.

What to watch:

  • Equity swings from bond/equity fair-value moves (equity fell 4.4% in H1 FY2026 on bond prices even as profit rose)
  • Liabilities (policy reserves) growing faster than the investment assets backing them

equityStructure.title: Attributable equity vs total equity (incl. NCI)
equityStructure.content:
Shareholders' equity is the portion attributable to Sunshine Insurance Group's own H-share/domestic-share holders; total equity incl. NCI adds minority interests in partly-owned subsidiaries.

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: the gap is minority interests in Sunshine AMC (~80%-owned) and Sunshine Surety (~87%-owned) -- a widening gap means profit growth at those subsidiaries accrues partly to outside shareholders, not to the group's H-share holders. The DCF values the attributable (per-share) measure.

What to watch:

  • NCI share of total equity trending up (dilutes per-share value even if consolidated metrics look strong)
  • Whether subsidiary-level profit growth is disproportionately NCI's

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income attributable to equity owners divided by the weighted-average share count (11,502m, basic = diluted, held flat -- no convertibles or share schemes disclosed).

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: EPS rose RMB0.27 to RMB0.41 H1-on-H1 (+38.5%), ahead of the FY2025 full-year RMB0.55; H shares and domestic unlisted shares rank pari passu for dividends, so EPS is calculated on the full 11,502m share count, not just the H-share float.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth tracking net income growth (share count is flat, so little dilution risk)
  • Dividend payout ratio against the regulator's solvency constraints, not just earnings

fcf.title: Owner FCF: distributable-earnings proxy, not operating-company free cash flow
fcf.content:
An insurer has no capital-expenditure-based "free cash flow" -- cash from operations is dominated by premium inflows and investment-portfolio movements, not a stay-in-business reinvestment cycle. The DCF instead uses profit before tax less finance costs on the capital supplementary bonds as its owner-earnings base, and net debt is held at zero (the convention this folder applies to insurers/banks, since the bonds' coupon is already inside profit before tax and repo liabilities fund the investment book, not the company).

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: net profit attributable to equity owners (not Owner FCF) is the primary earnings line to track against the valuation -- it rose 15.7% in FY2025 and 38.5% YoY in H1 FY2026, driven by VNB growth and improving P&C underwriting rather than cash conversion.

What to watch:

  • Net profit trend vs embedded value and VNB growth (the insurance-specific value drivers)
  • Solvency ratios (comprehensive/core), which constrain how much of that profit can ultimately be distributed

margins.title: Net margin
margins.content:
Net margin here is net income attributable to equity owners divided by total revenue (IFRS 17 insurance revenue plus net investment income and other income) -- there is no cost-of-revenue or gross-margin concept for an insurer.

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: net margin improved to 10.1% in H1 FY2026 from 7.5% a year earlier, helped by the 'New Sunshine Strategy' cost program (fixed costs -9.8% YoY in FY2025) and the P&C combined ratio improving to 98.9% ex-guarantee business.

What to watch:

  • Margin driven by underwriting improvement vs one-off investment gains (China A-share/bond swings)
  • The guarantee-insurance wind-down removing a historical drag (129% combined ratio, RMB1.51bn underwriting loss in FY2025)

profit.title: Net income vs total equity (incl. NCI)
profit.content:
Net income (attributable) is profit after tax, minority interests and one-offs belonging to Sunshine's own shareholders. Total equity incl. NCI is the capital base (including minority interests in Sunshine AMC and Sunshine Surety) that profit is earned against -- the closest insurer analogue to a bank's capital ratio.

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: weighted-average ROE improved to 8.3% in H1 FY2026 from 5.7% a year earlier even as total equity fell 4.4% on bond fair-value marks -- profit growth and equity moves can run in opposite directions in a period when bond yields move.

What to watch:

  • ROE trend (profit relative to the equity base), not just the absolute profit number
  • Equity swings from AFS/FVOCI bond and equity revaluations, which are not earnings

revenue.title: Total revenue vs IFRS 17 insurance revenue
revenue.content:
Total revenue (the CSV/DCF scaling base) is IFRS 17 insurance revenue plus net investment income and other income. IFRS 17 insurance revenue is only the service-margin/expense recognition each period, not premiums written -- it is much smaller than gross written premiums (GWP RMB150.7bn in FY2025 vs insurance revenue of RMB65.1bn).

For Sunshine Insurance Group Company Limited: management's own operating KPIs are GWP (+17.4% FY2025) and value of new business (VNB, +48.2% FY2025) -- neither is on this chart because GWP/VNB are not in the CSV; insurance revenue is the closest IFRS-reported proxy for top-line momentum.

What to watch:

  • Insurance revenue growth decoupling from total revenue growth (signals investment income, not underlying business, driving the total)
  • Interim rows for H1/H2 seasonality in investment income

dcf.base_sublabel: Profit before tax less capital-bond finance costs — net debt held at zero (insurer convention)
